text:
Dubai registered 10,195 residential sales worth AED 27,672,330,524 in the last four weeks, a 6.1% decline in volume compared to the previous period. Mortgage registrations totaled 4,054, recorded separately from sales. The off-plan share of transactions stood at 59.4%, down from 66.6% in the prior four weeks.

The median residential price per square foot decreased to AED 1,666, representing an 1.8% drop from the previous four-week median of AED 1,697. Top performing areas by sales volume over twelve weeks include Dubai South with 3,790 transactions and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,327. Business Bay recorded a median price of AED 2,108 per square foot, while Al Hebiah Fifth showed a 6.5% price decline over the same period.

Rental activity saw 87,085 contracts registered with a 49.6% renewal share. The median residential rent is AED 70,900 annually. Estimated gross yields are highest in Zaabeel First at 9.3% for flats, followed by International City Phase 1 at 8.6%. Dubai Production City offers a 6.4% yield with a median rent of AED 64,000.

Watch-list indicators show Al Yufrah 1 heating with a 36.5% price increase, while Palm Jumeirah cooled by 20.3%. Dubai Industrial City prices rose 11.3% with a 95.7% off-plan share. The anomaly monitor flagged 1,040 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35% away from comparable medians. Figures are based on registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial-share transfers, portfolio blocks, mortgages, gifts, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
